subject: Action: per-route audit snapshots + triage runbook
messages:
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: per-route audit snapshots + triage runbook

Ben —

Following our roadmap sync, product wants a lightweight, exportable "audit snapshot" for individual routes that we can hand to CS/SRE during a customer escalation or use to review recent regressions. The ask is not a full trace viewer; we need a compact, repeatable artifact that contains:

- 30-day summary (tokens, requests, cost) for a single route
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and recent tail spikes with timestamps
- Sample request+response payloads (sanitized) and associated trace IDs
- Model variant, quantization profile, batching config active at time of spike
- Pointer to KV cache hit rates and recent prefix cache deltas

Desired UX: button on a route page "Generate audit snapshot" -> produces a CSV + JSON summary and pins the route for 7 days in the console with an auto-generated triage checklist. Retention for snapshots should default to 90 days.

Attached is a short mock CSV and a triage template (triage-runbook-template.md) that illustrates expected fields. Can your team scope effort and give an estimate? Key requirements from PM: exportable, low-cost to produce (no heavy per-request replays), and links back to traces.

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Attachments: per-route-audit-sample_export.csv (stub), triage-runbook-template.md (stub)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: per-route audit snapshots + triage runbook

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear brief. This is something instrumentation and Console can support without a full trace replay pipeline if we limit the snapshot to aggregated metrics + a capped number of sample payloads (say up to 5 per snapshot) and links to trace IDs in the retention window. High-level plan:

1) Prototype a snapshot exporter that queries route-level aggregated tables (token counts, cost by model variant, p50/p95/p99) and bundles up to 5 recent sanitized samples with trace ids.
2) Add a console action to generate and download the snapshot and to pin the route (7d) + create a triage checklist from your template.
3) Hook an SRE preview step so we don't accidentally blow up DB costs for large tenants — by default snapshots will sample at the tenant slice.

Open questions:
- Which exact fields do PM/SRE want in the CSV header? I can align with the template but want a canonical list.
- For the KV cache metrics: do we need per-key deltas or is a hit-rate/sampled-key-list sufficient?
- Any customers (or segments) we should opt out initially?

Estimated work: 3 sprints to get an MVP (console action + export + checklist generator), assuming we can reuse the aggregation tables. If Marcus can confirm no infra blockers, I'll schedule a quick demo of the prototype the week of 3/26.

I can own the Console/UI changes; Marcus, can you confirm SRE capacity and the DB cost guardrails?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Product Ops Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

Ben / Kim —

We can take this on but a few constraints and suggestions from infra:

- DB cost: building per-request snapshots across large tenants will be expensive. Keep snapshots derived from the existing hourly aggregates and include sample IDs that map back to traces instead of replaying full traffic.
- KV cache: we should surface hit-rate plus a small sampled key-list (hash prefix) to avoid exporting secrets. Per-key deltas are expensive and rarely necessary for initial triage.
- Batching and concurrency: include the batching config that was active for the route in the snapshot (batch window ms, batch size distribution). That helps diagnose token-cost regressions.
- Chronology: snapshots should include a brief timeline (timestamped events) pointing to the top 3 spike windows with trace ids.

Suggested alternate: MVP = aggregated CSV + up to 5 sanitized samples + timeline + binding to existing trace ids. Post-MVP we can add a "replay-on-demand" P0 if product still needs it, but that should be gated behind quota & approvals.

I'll create an OBS ticket with proposed DB quota and a guard that prevents snapshots larger than 50MB and rate-limits per-tenant (see OBS-732). Also adding a small Lambda to scrub sample payloads for PII before download.

Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
